div.head: TO-DXY'S CUP-TIES.
div.p: TO-DXY'S CUP-TIES.

The first round of the Northern Union Cup-ties till be decided to-day, the following being the competing clubs : Warrington v. Batley. Swinton v. St. Helens. Liverpool City v. Hull. Wigan v. Hunslet. Hull Kingston Rovers v. Bradford. Oldham v. Runcorn Salford V. Leigh. Workington or Maryport v. Wakefield Trinity. Broughton Rangers v. Widnes. Huddersfield v. Brighouse St. James's. Leeds v. Rochdale Hornets. • 111illom v. Halifax. Barrow V. Dewsbury.

Keighley v. Brookland Rovers. -- Warrington will have the pleasure of entertaining their old Batley foes for the first time in a Cup-tie at Wilderspool. Three times previously have Batley knocked Warrington out of the Competition —in a semi-final at Huddersfield, in the final at Leeds, and in the first round last season at Batley. It is surely Warrington's turn to be avenged for all these reverses, and I feel confident they will extract compensation from to-day's encounter, even though their form of late has been far from encouraging. Batley have had a coin- paratively poor League season, and away from the beloved heights of Mount Pleasant they have generally proved easy victims. Warrington must not rate them too lightly, however. Batley in ordinary games and Batley in Cup-ties are two very different teams.

Though Warrington will not be quite at full strength they will have a good team in the field. Berry and Dickinson are both on the injured list as the result of the Halifax disaster, and the latter wiil probably be two or three weeks before his hand gets right. Fortunately Tilley has recovered from the sprain he got at Swinton, or the club would have been in difficulties for a full back. The most serious loss is that of Lees, who is unwell and did not wish to play. Hockenhall has to fill the vacancy, and unless Ile gets the ball away inure smartly than of late he will prove a poor partner for Jenkins. Belton takes the place of Preston, whose goal-kicking and general play have both deteriorated.

The selected Warrington team is : Tilley, full back ; Fish, Isherwood, Taylor, and Brooks, three- quarters ; Jenkins and Hockenhall, half backs ; Boardman, Thomas, Heath, .Shugars, Harmer and Belton, forwards.

The Batley team will be :—White, back ; Hanford, Will Davies, Senior, and " Waffle " Davies, three- quarter backs ; Edwards and Bevan, half backs ; Hill, Kitson, Settle, Farrar, Hodgson and Phillips, forwards.

div.head: STOCKTON HEATH SCHOOL DIFFICULTY.
div.p: STOCKTON HEATH SCHOOL DIFFICULTY.
Probable Settlement.

, The final meeting of the year of the Stockton Heath ' Parish Council was held at the Hall Cafe on Thursday evening when there were present: Messrs. J. W. Bouchier (presid. 1g). F. Pearson, H. J. Westbrook, J. Whitley, T. R. Westbrook, J. Hallows, J. H. Clarke, F. Warburton and E. Bradshaw (clerk). , The principal business to arise was the question of the school accommodation difficulty. This was intro- duced by a letter from the Board of Education in which they said :—Referring to your letter of 14th August 1905,1 am directed to state that the Board of Education after fully considering the matter are satisfied, on the facts brought before them, that the provision of a Council school in Stockton 'bath is necessary and they propose to decide accordingly. The only point which still appears to require consideration is the amount of accommodation to be allowed in the proposed school and the settlement of this question must to some extent depend on what decision the managers of the Stockton Heath National School come to in regard to the improvement of that school. In regard to this point the Board have made full local inquiry through H. 51. Inspector and have received a special report on the premises from their travelling architect which was communicated to the managers on ' the 22nd Februnry, 1006, and in the absence of any I definite action on the part of the managers the Board have now informed them and the local education authority that their recognition of the school will cease on 31st May, 1908, unless in the meantime a satisfactory scheme of improvement has been approved by the Board and is in course of being carried out with due dispatch. The Board notice that your petitioners ask that a local inquiry may be held before the matter is disposed of and I am now to inquire whether, in view of what has been already stated in this letter your petitioners are still desirous that such inquiry should be held and whether they are prepared to give security for the expense of such inquiry. Unless a reply is reeeived within a fortnight from the date a this letter (March 4th, the Board will proceed to decide that the proposed Council school for a number of children not exceeding 800 is necessary, leaving the authority to submit plans for any less number that they think fit." Mr. Bouchier,who is co-opted manager of St. Thomas' school, said the architect employed by the school anagers had visited the schools, and his report was to be submitted to the managers the following evening. As was well known it was their intention to try and have the existing schools altered as to accommodate 450 scholars, and in that case a new school for 500 would be ample to meet the requiiements of the parish. If the plans were approved by the school managers and the County Education Committee there was an end to the matter. They wished to avoid the erection of a school for 800 for many reasons, but mainly to keep down the rates.

Mr. Pearson: What is the present accommodation of the schools, presuming they could not be altered? Mr. Bouchier : The Board will not recognize the schools as accommodating any. The cost of the proposed alterations will probably run to £l,OOO. With regard to the letter I thought that as a matter of course an enquiry would be held.
Mr. Bradshaw exp ame , in answer to a question, that the Council, with the consent of the ratepays could spend a 3d. rate on the inquiry. Mr. Warburton thought a Parish meeting should be held.
Mr. Bouchier, answering Mr. Whitley, said that in Stockton Heath they had to find accommoda.tion for 850 scholars.

Mr. Whitley said he understood that the number was larger. A.member of the Education Committee had told him that they would be very unwise if they built a school to accommodate only 500. Mr. Bouchier : The school could be built in such a way that it could be extended without unduly increas- ing the cost. -
Whitley: It is understood that the managers will provide accommodation for 450. Mr. Pearson: We have no assurance that that is so.
Mr. Whitley: But we have every confidence in them.

Mr. H. J. Westbrook said they found that scholars from other districts came to the schools in Stockton Heath and they thought those matters should be taken into consideration at an inquiry. From the Board's letter it seemed to him that there was very little for them to do, and until they knew what the managers of St. Thomas schools were going to do they could do nothing. A school for SOO would not be built unless the Board ceased to recognizing the existing schools. He did not think an inquiry was necessary. If the danagers decided to alter their schools they would be satisfied. If not they would have to build a school for 800. Mr. Clarke said it appeared to him that the settle- ment of the question depended upon the action of the school managers, and until they knew what the action was going to be they were not in a position to do anythinrr. One point in the letter which astounded him, and which he regarded as a great piece of presump- tion, was that the Stockton Heath Parish Council should be asked to give security for the expense of the inquiry. They were fighting the battle not only of the people in Stockton Heath but of Walton, Latchford, Appleton, and in fact of the whole county and if there was an inquiry they were going to be mulcted in the whole of the costs. He protested against the Council being asked to pay the costs, as these should be borne by the Education department of the Cheshire County Council. Mr. Bouchier pointed out that three parishes— Stockton Heath, Walton, and Latchford Without—had been scheduled. They wanted Appleton and Warrington included as both those places would benefit by the schools.

Mr. H. J. Westbrook moved " That the Clerk be in- structed to acknowledge the letter from the Board of Education and to intimate that this Council under- stand that a scheme is being matured by the trustees and managers of St. Thomas's Church school to meet the requirements of the local education administrative sub-committee which the Council believes will obviate the necessity for any format inquiry being held, or for any further opposition by this Council. Pending the completioc of the scheme the Council desires to ask that their position and rights in regard to the proposed school may remain in abeyance and that the Board of Education will grant the Council the further time which may be required under the circumstances." Mr. Warburton seconded and the resolutions was unanimously approved. SHIP CANAL HOARDINGS.

The Clerk reported that in accordance with a resolu- tion passed at the Parish meeting, he had written to the nanchester Ship Canal Co., with respect to the removal of the advertisement hoardings at the Swing Bridge. He had received a reply stating that the matter would have attention.

div.head: CETAIRMAN THANKED.
div.p: CETAIRMAN THANKED.
At the conclusion of the meeting Mr. J. W. Bonchier was heartily thanked for his services in the chair during the past two years.

div.head: LATE CHIEF CONSTABLE. -- Watch Committee's Resolution.
div.p: THE LATE CHIEF CONSTABLE. -- Watch Committee's Resolution.

The death of the Chief °constable was formally reported to the Watch Committee on Thursday and a resolution expressing high appreciation of his services as an officer of the Corporation was passed. The meet- ing also expressed deep sympathy with Mrs. Talbot in her _bereavement.
The Commit-tee hare made a grant to the widow out the superannuation fund of an amount equal to one month's pay for each of ten completed years approved service.
Latest particulars about Mr. Talbot's death will be found on page 3.

div.head: Bridge-street Improvements.
div.p: Bridge-street Improvements.

The Corporation have come to terms with the executors of the late Mr. Joseph Shaw for the acquisition of the last lot of property which the Cor- poration have to purchase in Bridge-street. Mr. Shaw's executors will forthwith commence to re-build on a site in the rear of the existing premises.

div.head: Shorthand Writers' Association.
div.p: Shorthand Writers' Association.

The weekly meeting of the above association vras held at the Winnaarleigh Cafe on Wednesday night, when there was a good attendance. Speed prabtice was conducted as usual ; after which, a paper entitled " The T.P.S. Teachers' Diploma "was given by the enthusiastic hon, secretary of the Association, Mr. j. Marsh, 11.1 P.S. The lecturer, who recently passed the Teachers' Examination of the Incorporated Phono- graphic Society, gave an interesting account of the examination generaPy, and explained the various testg to which candidates had to submit themselves. It was evident, from his remarks, that the would-be- certificated shorthand teacher in this society must possess a sound knowledge of the Phonographic "why and wherefore." The paper was very instruc.- trve, and a hearty vote of thanks was accorded Mr. Marsh.

div.head: OUR LOCAL CaURCHES.
div.p: OUR LOCAL CaURCHES.
l(Cont;nued from Page 6.)

Services for Sunday. Bold-street Wesleyan Church: Preachers, 10.30, Rev. J. Gunnel; 6.30, Rev. J. Manning. Bewsey-road Wesleyan Church: Preachers, 10.30,Rev. E. J. Gawne 6.30, Rev. S. Pitt. Wycliffe Congregational Church: Preacher, 10.30 and 6.30, Rev. John, Yonge. Evening subject: "What is sin ?"

_ Golborne-street Baptist Church : Preacher, Rev. A. Harvey (Widnes). Subjects: 10.30, "The fool's epitaph " ; "The ultimate triumph of Christianity." Latchford Baptist Church: Preacher, Rev. J. F. Matthews. Subjects: 10.30, "My Son—thy Brother"; 6.0, "The ultimate religion." Parish Church : Special service for men at three o'clock in the afternoon will be addressed by the Rev. Canon Scott Holland, whose subject will be" I can and I can't. Visit of the Dean of Manchester.

The last of the series of addresses to men will be delivered at the Parish Church next Friday evening by Bishop Welldon, the newly-appointed Dean of Man- chester, who will take for his subject 'The Atone- ment." Bishop Welldon was at one time headmaster of the great public school at Harrow, and he has also served as Bishop of Calcutta.

Bold-street Wesleyan Church. During the week the organ which for many years has done duty in Bold-street Wesleyan Church, has been dismantled to make way for a new and more powerful instrument, which it is expected will be opened in June. The Church has also been closed for re-decoration and extensive structural alteration, and pending the re-open- ing the services will be conducted in the schools.—On Sunday night a special musical service was held, and was attended by a large congregation. Mr. F. Hickman presided at the organ and gave a number of selections, and cornet contributions were rendered by Messrs. Rutter and Clayton. Mrs. Arthur Booth sang very ably "God who made earth and Heaven."

div.head: Wycliffe P.S.A.
div.p: Wycliffe P.S.A.

There was a fair attendance at the Wycliffe P.S.A. meeting on Sunday. Mr. R. Atkinson presided, and stated that the organ fund had been closed. They had the pleasure of handing over to the treasurer of Wycliffe Church £5O towards the cost of repairing and improving the instrument. (Applause).—Mr. William Beswick moved, and Mr. McEachren seconded, "That the thanks of the brotherhood be given to all the officers who have so willingly collected that amount week by week." The resolution was carried. Twenty-four new members joined the society, making a total for the second Sunday in the new year of 339. Mr. Adcock, of Manchester, was the speaker. Mr. Cotton read the lesson. Mr. Payton contributed an organ solo, which was muela appreciated.

div.head: SHIP CANAL BILL.
div.p: THE SHIP CANAL BILL.
Clauses for the Protection of Warrington

The Manchester Ship Canal Bill has been reported to the House of Lords, read a third time, and sent down to the Commons. It will in due course be referred to a Committee. The Bill, as amended in Committee contains clauses defining the height of the spoil banks at Arpley, provision for the preservation of the exist- footpath, and the construction of the intended new road across the river diversion near Stag bridge. Clauses with regard to the prevention of further obstrac- tion of water from the river and for protection in case the water in the river should become more brackish were refused by the House of Lords.

You may rely upon me to study economy so as not to add unnecessarily to the expenditure of the town. I am, Yours sincerely, AGNES SIMPSON, 1.04, Bewsey-road, March 11th, 19,07.

HIACCTION OP GUARDIANS. TO THE BLECTOR OF BEW6EY WARD. LADIRB AND GENTLEMEN, \ My term of office having expired. I have much pleasure in again offering you my services as your representative. During the past six years I have, to the best of my ability, done my duty as a Guardian of the Poor, as evidenced by the large number of attendances I have made at the various Board and Committee Meetinaa My reason for being so particular ix attending is, tnat I have been better able to follow from week to week the business done by the Board, and so obtain a thorough grip of every transaction that has taken place. I am strongly opposed to any new extensions at the Workhouse Or the Homes at Padgate, also to any site being selected for the proposed New Offices for the Board outside our own land. These schemes alone, if prevented, will mean a saving to the Ratepayers of close upon £40.000, In conclusion, if you do me the honour to again elect me I can assure you that your confidence will not be mis- placed, as it is my sole ambition to serve the poor and aged people of the town in the most kind and considerate manner. Thanking you for past favours, I remain, Your most obedient Servant, JAMES PAYrON. 65, 67, Allen Street. Warrington.

BOARD OF GUARDIANS ELECTRIN. TO THE ELECTORS OF TOWN HALL WARD. LADIES AND GENTLF.MEN,— MY EARNEST WORK FO q THE SICK AND POOR I TRUST JUSTIFIES MT APPEAL FOR YOUR SUPPORT AT THE POLL. Yours faithfully, ALT. J. JOLLEY.

COUNTY BOROULtH OF WARFUNGTON. ELECTION OF GUMIDIANg. 'TO THE ELECTORS OF THE TOWN HALL WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, At the request of a large number of Ratepayers in the Ward and of several Public Bodies and Friendly iocietles in the town I have after careful consideration allowed myself to be nominated as the Representative of the Ward on the Board of Guardians. I am strongly opposed to the proposed erection of the New Poor Law Offices believi .g as I do that the time Is not opportune for the spending of some Four Thousand Pounds of the Ratepayers' money on a scheme that is illadvisen and promoted purely to satisfy tne peculiar fails of several members of the late Board. The Proposed Extension of the Workhouse which has been repeatedly advocated is wholly unnecessary, and it elected I should strongly oppose any such scheme being carried into effect, lam a strong believer in out-relief to the poor and would use my best endeavours to encourage the adoption of this systems instead of forcing the ~ged and poor in.o the Union,separating husband and wife,clothing them in Workhouse garb, and causing tham unnecessary suffering by breaking up their homes. I am strongly opposed to Guardians hiring the services of inmates of she Union to do work for them at their homes at a sweating wal,e. The cost of management in connection with the administration of the Poor Law is enormous and requires careful watching. Ido not seek your confidence as a stranger, has ing lived amongst you all try life, and should I be successful at the Poll on the 25th of March you may depend that I will endeavour to carry out my duties to your entire satisfaction. I am, Ladies and Gentlemen. Your Obedient Servant. ALFRED B. MARSH. 3, Rolleston St.. Warrington.
